newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air France plans cargo deal MAS.
newsitem.headline: Air France plans cargo deal MAS.

text.p: Air France Cargo said it planned a cargo deal with Malaysian Airline System Bhd to target the fast-growing Malaysia market.
Francois Bachelet, executive vice president and chief operating officer, told Reuters the deal with MAS was a first step in building a global network of cargo partnerships.

Speaking after a Frankfurt cargo reception, Bachelet said a joint venture would be started with MAS to service Malaysian destinations such as Penang since Air France only had traffic rights for twice-weekly flights.
"We are going to guarantee a two-day service from Europe to Malaysia through Paris and Kuala Lumpur," he said.
"The idea is to work out with MAS a sort of small hub concept in KL whereby we would pre-forward there freight that we do not have rights to sell now, and they could use Paris," he added.
Bachelet did not indicate when the joint venture could be launched.
But he stressed: "We are not going to hub into Kuala Lumpur all the freight we have for south-east Asia."
Air France would maintain and expand its bilateral deals with Thai Airways International, Singapore Airlines, Korean Airlines and Japan Airlines, he added.
The French carrier was also considering operating freighter services into Dubai to connect to the Asian services of other airlines, Bachelet said.
This could work similarly to the back-to-back freighter flights of Lufthansa Cargo and Singapore Airlines which connected at Sharjah, he noted.
